name: astro-xai-bench
description: Explainable artificial intelligence (xAI) methods are increasingly used to interpret machine learning classifiers of astronomical transients, yet their reliability is rarely assessed quantitatively. We present astro-xai-bench , an open benchmark that evaluates explanation quality along five complementary axes – perturbation-based faithfulness, deletion and insertion AUC, complexity, cross-representation plausibility, and the standard model- and data-randomisation sanity checks – applied to nine classifiers spanning tree-based, deep-learning, and physics-informed architectures on the PLAsTiCC photometric transient dataset (14 classes, six passbands), with all metrics averaged over five random seeds. A detailed case study of XGBoost (tree-based) and CNN2D (convolutional on Gramian angular field images) illustrates how each xAI axis interacts with model architecture: faithfulness is representation-dependent, complexity rankings invert under basis change, and projected plausibility is sensitive to the projection rather than the model.
